title: Calls, shops and restaurants
point: Handle calls and video meetings, and ask for what you need in shops, restaurants and clinics, with the fixed phrases people use every day.

sentences.ja: ミュートになってますよ。
sentences.note: "I think" makes it a gentle heads-up rather than a correction.

sentences.ja: 画面、ちゃんと見えてますか？
sentences.text: Can you see my screen okay?

sentences.ja: すみません、もう一度言っていただけますか？
sentences.text: Sorry, could you say that again?
sentences.note: This works anywhere; a quick "Sorry?" also does the job.

sentences.ja: 少々お待ちいただけますか？
sentences.text: Could you hold on a moment?
sentences.note: On the phone, "hold on" means stay on the line.

sentences.ja: 後でかけ直してもいいですか？
sentences.text: Can I call you back later?
Could we get the check, please?
sentences.note: "Check" is American; British English says "the bill".

sentences.ja: これの別のサイズはありますか？
sentences.text: Do you have this in a different size?
sentences.note: "Have this in" plus a size or color is the set shop phrase.
The question asks if it's taken, so "No" means you can sit down.

sentences.ja: 昨日から頭痛がひどいんです。
sentences.text: I've had a bad headache since yesterday.
